correctness.rationale: Exact normal equations yield E1=(X·Y/||X||²)(U·V/||U||²) as independent G/chi factors, proving moments from gamma integrals. Independent rows yield E2=(ΣW_iZ_i)/(ΣW_i²) with W,Z iid products of independent Gaussians. The product-normal K0 density has a logarithmic singularity at 0, and spherical-polar integration with integrable angular logs gives t^-R(log t)^R; layer cake yields the boundary p=R divergence. Dense error is G/chi_R, giving pure t^-R tail. Conditioning on W then on first Gaussian factors and strict Jensen establishes E(E2²)>1/(R-2) if R>2. Independently recomputed C1=4/π²,C2=1/π,C4=3/π² by product normal moments. Explicit argument covers R=1 and R=2 and dimension independence, with no implication that four rows cost identical runtime.
